alice: FYI - Prospect (CapitalGrid) wants Redwood Private in their cloud with connections from on-prem proxy. Must-haves: (1) original client IP visible to their SIEM, (2) deny-by-default egress. They want minimal network changes. Thoughts?

ben: Short: three practical patterns - PrivateLink (fast approvals, endpoint ENI NATs client IP), VPC Peering (preserves IP, needs routing/peering approvals), or TGW/DirectConnect (best control for multi-location). If they insist on network-layer client IP, peering or TGW is required.

ravi: If application-level attribution suffices, we can emit signed X-Forwarded-For headers or enable Proxy Protocol on an NLB we manage. That avoids peering but requires app/proxy changes to consume headers. Also flag: if their egress inspects TLS, recommend exempting our FQDN so SNI reaches destination.

ben: Pasteable firewall snippet (recommend FQDN first, CIDR fallback):
```
# Outbound from corporate firewall/proxy to Redwood PrivateDeploy
ALLOW tcp 443 -> private.redwood-inference.net  # control plane + APIs
ALLOW tcp 443 -> models.redwood-inference.net   # model pulls (scheduleable)
ALLOW tcp 443 -> telemetry.redwood-inference.net # optional
# CIDR fallback (we will provide final prefixes): ALLOW tcp 443 -> 198.51.100.0/22
```

alice: Pricing ask: at ~5TB/mo which pattern is cheaper?

ravi: Rough, non-binding estimate: PrivateLink: ~$0.025-0.065/GB + endpoint-hour; Peering/TGW: ~$0.006-0.035/GB but customer bears DirectConnect/VPN costs. In short, peering/TGW often cheaper at volume; PrivateLink easier for security/compliance.

netops-bot: :white_check_mark: sandbox-capgrid provisioned (us-west-2). Drive: https://drive.redwood/capgrid-poc (creds in secret manager).

alice: Action items: ben -> 1-page decision table + cost bullets. ravi -> firewall text + questionnaire snippet about client identity and TLS inspect. Send to customer in 24h.

ben: On it.
